territorial_scope.description: Applies to the Department of Veterans Affairs, its Secretary and employees, and claimants for VA disability benefits; no extraterritorial reach is stated.

evidence.quote: Section 714 of title 38, United States Code, is amended--

summary.short: Would expedite disciplinary actions against VA employees, raise criminal penalties for fraud and misconduct involving veterans' benefits, set whistleblower investigation and incentive rules, mandate annual ethics training, and require the VA Secretary to review the disability rating schedule and build AI tools to flag claims subject to human review.
summary.long: As introduced, the CLEAN VA Act amends titles 38, 18 and 5 of the U.S. Code. Section 2 sets factors for removal, demotion or suspension of VA covered individuals, requires review for substantial evidence, limits administrative judge, Merit Systems Protection Board and court review of penalties, and sets 15-business-day and 7-business-day timing limits. Section 3 adds penalties for VA-employee offenses under 18 U.S.C. 641, 1001, 201 and 1920, including imprisonment terms and fines stated in the text, forfeiture of federal annuity benefits under 5 U.S.C. 8312, a 60-day deadline for whistleblower retaliation investigations, annual settlement reporting, and incentive awards of up to $10,000. Section 4 directs the VA Secretary to review the disability rating schedule and develop data analytics and AI systems to flag claim irregularities, with human review required before administrative or disciplinary action; a report is due within 180 days. Section 6 repeats that text. Section 5 requires annual ethics and fraud training under new 38 U.S.C. 7735, overseen by the Inspector General.

notes: Text as introduced; the bill is pending and no consolidated text is given. Sec. 4 and Sec. 6 repeat the same disability-rating review and AI/data-analytics provisions; Sec. 6(d) says Not later than 180 days while Sec. 4(d) says Not later that (typo). Possible internal conflict in 38 U.S.C. 714(b): (b)(1) caps notice, response and final decision at 15 business days in aggregate, while (b)(2) sets a 7-business-day response period and (b)(3)(A) allows 15 business days after notice for the final decision.
